content: While specific historical protocols from the 2020 to 2024 period remain sparsely documented in broader literature, recent industry practices highlight a strong commitment to emergency preparedness. For instance, recent emergency response practices in the mining industry were demonstrated through a mass-casualty drill conducted by Kumba Iron Ore at its Sishen Airfield [45] . Such exercises underscore the industry's operational safety priorities and the critical need for seamless stakeholder engagement during crisis scenarios [45] . Comparison of Dispatch and Emergency Communication Systems in South African Mining System Type Primary Focus Key Technologies & Protocols Main Operational Benefit Dispatch & Control Room Systems Operations management and resource allocation Fleet management software, SCADA, Two-way radio integration Operational efficiency and centralized monitoring Emergency Communication Systems Miner safety and incident response Underground distress beacons, TETRA, Evacuation PA systems Safety assurance and rapid emergency resolution Data Source: Google Search Regulatory Standards and Compliance under MHSA The South African mining communications market operates within a highly dynamic sector that is continuously shaped by technological advancements, production trends, and broader global industry factors. Parallel to technological advancements, the regulatory landscape governing mining operations in South Africa is stringent, particularly concerning the Mine Health and Safety Act (MHSA). The MHSA predominantly pertains to occupational health and safety in mines, ensuring that all operational facets, including the deployment of telecommunications infrastructure, adhere to rigorous safety protocols to protect personnel in hazardous environments. As of June 2026, available information regarding MHSA compliance explicitly within South Africa's telecommunications sector is limited, and much of the analyzed content does not directly address the specifics of this regulatory intersection. The application of the MHSA to telecommunications is often tangential or sector-specific, primarily triggered when infrastructure installation occurs within hazardous mining areas. Despite the limited explicit documentation in broader telecommunications regulations, the operational reality within the mining sector shows a strong commitment to regulatory adherence.
